record.title: China's culture ministry approves 14 AI application pilots across culture and tourism
record.summary: China's Ministry of Culture and Tourism published an approved roster of 14 AI+culture-and-tourism pilot projects. The official attachment names implementing and recommending units and groups projects across six directions, including cultural production, public services, heritage protection, tourism formats and services, and market supervision. Named implementers include national cultural organizations, universities, public bodies and companies. The document records project approvals; it gives no funding, milestones, technical specifications or outcomes, so it does not establish that systems have been deployed or produced measurable benefits.
organizations: Ministry of Culture and Tourism of China

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The Ministry of Culture and Tourism's official attachment lists 14 approved AI+culture-and-tourism pilot projects, with project names, directions, implementing units and recommending units.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The 14 projects span six listed directions: cultural/art production; public cultural services; cultural heritage protection; new culture-and-tourism formats; tourism services and governance; and culture/tourism market supervision.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The notice and attachment do not establish project funding, technical design, implementation progress, deployment, measured user outcomes or economic impact.

evidence_gaps.description: The notice and roster assign pilot projects but provide no budgets, milestones, procurement details, technical specifications or progress evidence.
No measured outputs, service-quality changes, user outcomes, costs or economic effects are reported.

brief.importance_rationale: If implemented, a ministry-approved cohort of 14 projects across six cultural and tourism directions could show how China's AI+ agenda is translated into sector-specific public-service, heritage, creative and tourism applications. The official list establishes approvals and assigned units, not implementation, funding, technical performance or economic effects.
limitations: The evidence is a ministry notice and its official attachment; it establishes an approved project roster, not completed implementation.
The attachment provides project names, directions and responsible units but no funding amounts, schedules, technical designs, model choices or evaluation plans.
The roster is a selected cohort and does not establish adoption prevalence across China's culture and tourism sectors or causal economic impact.
organizations: Ministry of Culture and Tourism of China

technical.claimed_result: The ministry-approved roster names 14 projects across six application directions; the source does not quantify AI performance or deployment outcomes.
technical.demonstrated_result: The official notice and attachment document approval of 14 named pilot projects and identify implementing and recommending units. No deployment was independently inspected.
technical.mechanism: The notice says projects were selected after applications, recommendations, review and on-site inspection, and instructs recommending units to supervise implementation. The attachment groups the approved projects by application direction.
technical.regime: China's Ministry of Culture and Tourism AI+culture-and-tourism application-pilot cohort, published 2026-10-16. Evidence is administrative approval and roster contents only.
technical.strongest_baseline: No before/after or matched comparison is provided; the source describes selected projects, not impact relative to non-selected units or prior service baselines.

brief.title: China's culture ministry approves 14 AI application pilots across culture and tourism
brief.why_it_matters: The roster gives a concrete view of how a national AI policy is being directed into cultural and tourism tasks, including heritage, public services and visitor-facing applications. It can guide follow-up on sector adoption and implementation, but approval is not deployment: budgets, technical designs, milestones and results remain unreported in the inspected notice and attachment.
